title: Drop the Metals MCP fileInFocus workaround now that glob searches cover the whole workspace
body:
Metals 1.6.9 shipped scalameta/metals-feature-requests#464 (implemented in scalameta/metals#8776): `glob-search` and `typed-glob-search` now search the whole workspace when no `fileInFocus` is given, covering every module, the test targets, the `cli` and `experiments` executables, and dependencies.

Our agent instructions still carry the old workaround: the "Symbol tool file focus" section of `CLAUDE.md` tells agents to pass a `fileInFocus` to every Metals symbol tool and to query three representative files (`app`, `cli`, `experiments`) in parallel for a project-wide search. That costs context on every session and three calls per search.

## Scope

- Replace that section with "Symbol tool targets": the glob searches need no target; `get-usages`, `get-docs` and `get-source` take the owning module as `module` (derived from the "Packages" table in `docs/architecture/module-overview.md`, `<module>-test` for test code).
- `inspect` still returns no members when given `module` (or `searchAllTargets`) — reported as scalameta/metals#8880. Document its `fileInFocus` workaround in an on-demand doc, `docs/agents/metals-mcp-inspect-workaround.md`, to be deleted once that issue is fixed.
- Update the `scoverage-inspector` skill, which links to the old section.
- Make Metals 1.6.9 the minimum version in `docs/development/metals-mcp-claude-code-setup.md`, and explain how to upgrade a running stack.
